read_scope.notes: Read the complete extracted text of all 22 PDF pages, including references and Appendices A-G. Visually inspected all 22 rendered pages, including Figures 1-5 and Tables 1-10. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex for wording and locations. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth; the main narrative was assessed independently of their derivations. Extraction and rendering used the isolated directory /tmp/editorial-r06-b-rbhgk9v7. No other review records, earlier manuscript versions, progress records, or evaluation goals were read.

score_reasons.expression: The prose is precise, fluent and mostly economical. The opening Monet/Sisley proximity example, the three idealized generators in Section 4.1, and the explanation of the two ordering changes in Section 5.4 turn technical distinctions into readable statements. Terms such as contrast, aligned response, error and calibration are explained before they carry major claims. A localized concentration of inferential terminology in Section 4.3 could be lightened without sacrificing the method.
score_reasons.structure: The progression from a concrete question through the prompt design, interpretable feature families, metric intuition, estimation and results is exceptionally coherent. Section 5 has informative finding-based headings; primary intervals, descriptive pair analysis, calibration and source correction remain visibly distinct. Detailed derivations, alternative metrics, controls, supporting cohorts and provenance are appropriately placed in optional appendices. The source-correction comparison is surfaced in the main text and conclusion rather than left as a buried qualification.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract stands alone, the six prompt conditions and two repeats explain the 1,008-image design, and Table 1 translates the feature families into visual properties. Section 4.1 supplies both a measured lightness example and an intuitive error benchmark before notation. The manuscript clearly distinguishes the theoretical no-contrast predictor from the generic-painting arm, calibrated vectors from new images, and digital reference agreement from perceptual fidelity. Figure 2 provides useful magnified detail and Figure 3 makes pair-level heterogeneity interpretable, although the latter's small numerical annotations make some close comparisons less immediate at normal page size.
score_reasons.engagement: The central question has a discernible consequence for model evaluation, and the results sustain a narrative: most change is shared, detectable alignment can coexist with high error, some painter distinctions remain weak, and both calibration and scene treatment can change the ordering. Figure 1 offers substantial visual evidence to inspect, while Figures 2 and 3 expose different aspects of the labeled pattern. One bounded observation explicitly drawn from Figure 1 would make the image panel contribute more directly to the narrative rather than leaving all visual interpretation to the reader.

strengths: The introduction concretely explains why becoming closer to Monet and Sisley alike does not establish reproduction of the difference between them.
Section 4.1 gives intuition before notation: the actual lightness gap and the errors of no-response, exact-response and doubled-response generators establish what the two principal scores mean.
The primary result is stated with appropriate emphasis: all aligned-response intervals are positive, but no model is established to beat the no-contrast error benchmark.
Table 3 and its surrounding text explain why GPT Image 2 can benefit from shrinking a near-unit aligned response and why averaging scenes can reverse Nano Banana 2 and FLUX.
The source-correction section explicitly identifies the Sunburst comparison that ceases to be resolved and distinguishes a newly positive retrospective interval from a confirmatory finding.

Figures 1-3 are well integrated, with clear condition labels, matching reference-to-generated segments, a magnified three-painter view and numerical pair summaries. The appendix preserves technical depth without making it necessary to recover the main findings.

findings.location: Section 4.3, page 6; paper.tex, paragraph beginning “We compare models scene by scene”
findings.issue: The sentence equating the paired comparison with scene fixed-effects regression adds a second statistical formulation immediately before an already dense interval paragraph. The same equivalence is explained in Appendix B.2.
findings.reader_effect: A new reader briefly has to process an additional method name even though the scene-paired comparison is already sufficient to understand the analysis and results.
findings.suggested_change: Cut the main-text sentence beginning “In this balanced design” and retain its existing Appendix B.2 account. Keep the scene-pairing rationale, family size, adjustment, interval interpretation and uncertainty limitations in the main text. This is a local cut, not a request to remove necessary estimation details.

findings.issue: The annotated pair slopes and errors are appreciably smaller than the surrounding manuscript text, despite the figure being the main place where all pair-level values can be inspected together.
findings.reader_effect: The broad Monet-Sisley pattern is immediately visible, but checking distinctions such as -0.01 versus 0.07 or the small negative error requires enlargement of the page.
findings.suggested_change: Increase the cell-annotation and tick-label font sizes within the current figure footprint, using some of the spare vertical spacing around the two heatmaps if necessary. Preserve all six pairs, both metrics and the benchmark explanations; no extra figure or page is needed.

findings.issue: The image-panel introduction explains how the grid is organized but does not articulate a single concrete visual observation from it.
findings.reader_effect: The panel is attractive and useful, but the reader must independently discover how visible differences among named outputs connect to the paper's question about shared versus painter-specific responses.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the generic sentence about each model occupying one row with one short, explicitly scene-specific observation from the displayed images—for example, the darker outlined blue-green trees in GPT Image 2's Cézanne output compared with its lighter Monet and Sisley outputs. Present it as an illustration of the name response, without claiming visual proof of historical fidelity. A replacement preserves the 22-page limit and leaves the abstract unchanged.

summary: An excellent, self-contained editorial presentation of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The main narrative is readily understood, the figures and numerical examples support the distinction between response detection and target agreement, and inferential and perceptual limits are stated clearly. Remaining improvements are localized reductions in methodological friction and refinements to how the figures guide inspection; they do not require new evidence, longer text or a change in scope.
